items.title: Iran's attacks on US bases in the Middle East mark 'end of an era'
items.description: Five months into a war Donald Trump said would last only weeks, the Iran conflict has so far cost the United States tens of billions of dollars and brought about "the end of an era" in American military strategy.

items.title: Businesses sue Trump as he defends 'very standard tariffs'
items.description: Two small US businesses sue the US president to try to stop him from placing new tariffs on imports from scores of countries, including Australia.

items.title: Japan's popular princess sparks calls to ditch male-only succession law
items.description: There are only three people in line to inherit Japan's Chrysanthemum Throne, and one of them is 90 years old. All three of them are men.

items.title: Australia's 'monoculture' might be at the Labor conference
items.description: For those who believe in the virtue of converting and wrangling political trade-offs into a unified, coherent set of messages, Labor's example is transcendent.

items.title: A who's who of those at the centre of the ICAC's latest explosive probe
items.description: Eight weeks of public hearings by the corruption watchdog that could change the NSW Liberal Party forever begin on Monday. These are some of the key players embroiled in the donations investigation.

items.title: One Nation surge creates headache for the Coalition in Victoria's east
items.description: Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has campaigned in Gippsland this week, hoping to lure back voters who are turning towards a surging One Nation.

items.title: Quick hits: Aussie's dash to glory, Englishman drops his lollies
items.description: A broken lane rope holds up the swimming, an Australian wins gold after a mad dash from the medal podium, and an Englishman drops his lollies. Here are the quick hits from day one of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Bali bans two Dutch men alleged to have hosted discriminatory run club
items.description: Bali's Immigration department bans two Dutch expats from Indonesia for organising a run club event "fraught with discrimination against local residents".

items.title: India's Gen Z are filming 'fit checks' while running from police
items.description: Across the country's protest hotspots, India's gen Z are using meme culture as part of their hopes to bring the country into a new dawn.

items.title: They drink our water and take our power, but do data centres create jobs?
items.description: Data centres are in development across Australia, but how many jobs will these big, thirsty facilities actually support?

items.title: Chemical manufacturer ends sales of controversial herbicide
items.description: The chemical giant has ended sales in Australia and New Zealand, blaming new regulatory restrictions, as well as commercial, manufacturing and logistical challenges.

items.title: Tens of thousands flee fires in France, blazes merge outside Madrid
items.description: France orders total evacuation of Cap Ferret peninsula as Spain declares national emergency for the first time over fires.

items.title: The UK is banning high-caffeine drinks for under-16s. How does coffee compare?
items.description: The British government wants to ban the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to people under the age of 16. But how do they compare to coffee, tea and other beverages many people regularly consume? And what's the situation here in Australia?

items.title: Live: Waratahs meet Drua in Super Rugby Women's grand final
items.description: The Waratahs are chasing a seventh Super Rugby Women's title, but they face the daunting task of playing the Drua in Fiji. Follow live.

items.title: 'If you get cancer, you will go bankrupt': Anna Funder on life in the US
items.description: The award-winning author, who burst onto the literary scene with her debut, Stasiland, in 2003, discusses writing, AI and the rise of fascism.

items.title: ABC 5050 quiz: Testing your knowledge of L7's biggest hit, the Odyssey and rainbows made of fog
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Dog trainer says ABC's Muster Dogs is driving demand for working dogs
items.description: Gary White travels the world teaching people how to get the most out of their working dog. Lately, he's seen strong demand for working dogs, in part thanks to ABC's hit series Muster Dogs.

items.title: Will Hobart ever see snow as it did 40 years ago?
items.description: Forty years ago today, the heaviest winter snow in 65 years descended on Hobart, and while snow does make an appearance around the city these days, waking up to a winter playground in the backyard is far less likely, say experts.

items.title: Elders call for overhaul of 'tokenistic' governance on APY Lands
items.description: A group of elders on South Australia's remote Aṉangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) Lands say the region's current model of governance is failing — and have put forward plans for a major overhaul.

items.title: ICC dismisses prosecutor Karim Khan for serious misconduct
items.description: The International Criminal Court has dismissed prosecutor Karim Khan following an investigation into sexual misconduct allegations.

items.title: Four Palestinian villagers, 2 Israeli soldiers killed in West Bank clashes
items.description: Violent clashes in the occupied West Bank have left two Israeli soldiers and four Palestinian villagers dead.

items.title: LeBron's new teammates go wild as NBA star announces move
items.description: NBA legend LeBron James says he still has more to give after his shock announcement that he is headed to Philadelphia.

items.title: WA's famous Wave Rock is covered in tar and sediment from damaged wall
items.description: A fragile wall above one of Western Australia's most famous tourist attractions, Wave Rock near Hyden, has sparked debate among locals over whether it should be preserved or removed.

items.title: Tasmania Police says stabbing, fatal crash linked
items.description: Police were called to a house in Exeter, where they say a woman had received "serious stab wounds". A short time later, the man who police believe inflicted the wounds died in a car crash, which also left a third person seriously injured.

items.title: Man dead, police officer shot in domestic violence callout
items.description: Police were responding to a domestic violence incident west of Maryborough when a man allegedly opened fire on Friday night.
